fatal_errors: The proposed W-V-Nb material does not reconstruct the studied equimolar WTaTiVZr alloy.

It assumes a homogenized single-phase solid solution, whereas the target alloy was an as-cast, solidification-segregated two-BCC-phase material with W-Ta-rich dendrites and Zr-Ti-rich interdendritic regions.
It substitutes hypothetical tests above 1000 °C and under neutron irradiation for the actual room-temperature compression, room-to-500 °C indentation, and room-temperature scratch experiments.
It claims irradiation resistance and reduced long-lived activation without supporting evidence; neither irradiation behavior nor reactor-service activation was measured in the target study.
The categorical assertion that niobium does not generate long-lived activation products is scientifically unreliable, notably because neutron activation can produce long-lived Nb-94.
explanation: The response addresses the broad fusion-PFC theme and proposes a falsifiable comparative testing program, but it misses the target material, processing route, two-phase dendritic microstructure, experimental conditions, and quantitative mechanical results. Its generic expectation of better high-temperature strength than tungsten only weakly overlaps the reported outcome. Although it notes that reactor-relevant irradiation remains unverified, the central rationale nevertheless rests on unsupported irradiation and activation claims. The proposed experiment is reasonably discriminating for its own alternative hypothesis, but no cited evidence supports that hypothesis, and the W-V-Nb activation premise is questionable.
